reading.body:
Six interactive estimators cover the questions that decide whether an AI project is viable: token cost, GPU memory, context window fit, training cost, energy and carbon, and return on investment.

The set is organized around constraints rather than capabilities. GPU memory and context window fit determine whether a model can run on given hardware at all. Token cost and training cost determine what running it spends. Energy and carbon attach a physical input to that spend. Return on investment closes the loop by asking whether the spend is recovered.

For AI specifically, the inclusion of energy and carbon alongside VRAM and token cost reflects that inference and training draw power, and that power is a cost line rather than an externality. A reader weighing a deployment can see the arithmetic behind each estimate instead of a single opaque figure.

What the data does not contain is any calculator output, any worked example, or any stated range of inputs. It lists six tools and their subjects, and states that each shows its own arithmetic and what it excludes. It does not say how accurate the estimates are, what hardware or pricing assumptions they use, or whether they have been checked against measured results.
